title: Ops Sync Retro & SLO Migration Play — Q3 2026
body:
Overview:

This doc captures the playbook for the cross-functional SLO migration and the post-migration ops sync/retro cadence. Objective is to standardize SLO definitions across platform services, migrate alerts and dashboards to the new SLO schema, and run a short retro loop to capture operational learnings and follow-ups. This is intentionally pragmatic: decision rubric + minimal safe rollout path + rollback triggers.

Why now:
- Several teams have inconsistent SLO math and different alert thresholds (e.g., error budget vs p99 tail) leading to noisy paging and unclear ownership.
- Dedicated and hosted inference routes will soon share the same traffic router; having consistent SLOs reduces cross-mode incidents and supports automated routing fallback policies.

Goals (success criteria):
- All infra/platformed services adopt the unified SLO schema (latency p50/p95/p99, availability, and inference-error-rate) by end of Q3 with automated dashboards.
- Reduce paging noise by 30% (measured as >70% reduction in duplicate alerts across teams).
- Complete migration with a tested rollback for at least 90% of services.

Scope (in scope / out of scope):
- In scope: API gateway, model-serving controllers, cache layer, batch workers, telemetry ingestion.
- Out of scope: customer-managed private deployments (will be documented separately), data-plane model weights storage.

Timeline (high level):
- Week 0 (planning): alignment, finalize schema, target SLOs per service.
- Week 1–2 (staging migration): apply new SLOs to staging and enable dashboards + synthetic checks.
- Week 3 (canary migration): subset of traffic routed, oncall monitoring and war-room active.
- Week 4 (full migration): flip remaining services, monitor 72h.
- Week 6 (retro + follow-ups): ops sync retro, action tracker, schedule any longer-term platform changes.

Owners & RACI (primary contacts):
- Program lead: Nadia Patel (eng-sre) — overall coordination, exec updates.
- SLO design & validation: Samantha Chen (applied-ml) & Marco Alvarez (serving-runtime).
- Dashboards & alerts: Jonah Reed (observability).
- Rollout orchestration: Priya Nair (platform-engineering).
- Oncall war-room lead (week 3): Eliot Kim (site-reliability).

Migration checklist (minimal viable steps):
1) Finalize SLO schema document and quick-reference (owner: Samantha) — include exact metric names, windowing, and burn-rate math.
2) Map current service metrics -> target SLO metrics (owner: Marco) — produce per-service mapping table.
3) Create staging dashboards + synthetic traffic tests (owner: Jonah).
4) Update alert rules with temporary higher thresholds for canary (owner: Jonah + Priya).
5) Run canary with subset traffic (owner: Priya) and keep a dedicated war-room Slack channel + ephemeral Zoom.
6) Collect 72h burn-rate + pager noise metrics, decide to proceed/rollback (decision owner: Nadia).
7) Bulk migrate remaining services using orchestration script (owner: Priya).
8) Post-migration verification checklist (owner: Marco).
9) Populate post-mortem template if any SLO regressions occur (owner: Eliot).

Rollout safety and rollback triggers:
- Abort and rollback if: sustained burn-rate > 2x expected for 6 hours, repeated paging spikes (3 or more pages in 1h from same service), or if synthetic checks show >5% increased error rate.
- Rollback procedure: restore previous alerting config and dashboards, revert service SLO config via infra flag, notify stakeholders.

Monitoring & metrics (what we will track):
- SLO burn-rate per service (1h, 6h, 24h windows).
- Pager volume (pre/post migration) and duplicate page ratio.
- Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) slices by route, model, and region.
- Synthetic test pass rate across endpoints.

Communication plan:
- Pre-migration: email + #sre-announcements doc with migration schedule and expected impact.
- War-room channel: #slo-migration-warroom (temporary) — invite oncall and service leads.
- Exec update: 1-pager to CTO and VP Eng after canary with go/no-go recommendation.
- Post-migration: summary note with action items and SLO attainment dashboard links.

Ops sync + Retro template (to run Week 6):
- Start with incident summary logs and burn-rate trends.
- Collect: What went well, What surprised us, What should we change.
- Concrete follow-ups: tooling gaps, metric naming inconsistencies, alert tuning tasks.
- Assign owners + due dates, put high-impact items into product backlog.

Draft war-room play script (for canary window):
- T-30m: start synthetic checks and smoke tests, confirm oncall rotation.
- T=0: enable canary SLO config on subset routing.
- T+0–3h: observe burn-rate; keep watch on duplicates and paging.
- T+6h: decision checkpoint. If safe, expand to 25% traffic.
- T+24h: decision checkpoint to either proceed to full or rollback.

Retro notes & early learnings (notes-to-self style — from initial staging trial):
- Staging telemetry surface misses header-level breakdowns for model routing — added 'route_tag' label to metrics.
- Some services reported high p99 due to noisy downstream dependency; need isolation experiments.
- Alert suppression logic must include dedupe across alert sources (gateway + controller).

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- Do we standardize on 30d rolling window for availability SLO or keep 7d for experimental services? (tradeoff: sensitivity vs stability)
- How to represent tail-latency SLOs for batch workers where percentiles skew?
- Do we create a shared ops-runbook repo for SLO migrations vs per-team copies?

Action items (immediate):
- Marco: deliver per-service metric mapping CSV by 2026-07-16.
- Jonah: staging dashboards + synthetic checks in prometheus/grafana by 2026-07-18.
- Priya: deployment playbook + orchestrator script PR by 2026-07-20.
- Samantha: finalize SLO schema doc and short explainer by 2026-07-15.
- Nadia: schedule exec sync and prepare 1-pager for 2026-07-19.

Appendix: quick references and links to templates:
- SLO schema (link): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/SLO+Schema+v2 (canonical).
- Post-mortem template: /ops-templates/postmortem.md
- Alert dedupe RFC: https://docs.redwood.ai/rfc/alert-dedupe.

Notes about tone: this is a working doc — expect edits and action item churn. If you want changes to the rollback thresholds or canary percentages, drop a comment or ping Nadia.

Last-scratch notes (todo later):
- Run alert-simulator to validate dedupe.
- Put a small tagging job to retro-fit older metrics with 'route_tag' label.
